Overview

We are seeking an Electrical Engineering student interested in design validation, automated testing, and hands-on laboratory work. The intern will work with experienced test engineers to develop and improve test methods, write test code, integrate laboratory instruments, collect and analyze measurement data, and document results for high-power electronic test and measurement products.

The position provides exposure to automated test set development, environmental testing, custom test hardware, and high-voltage/high-power power supply systems operating up to 2 kV and up to 1 MW. All high-energy laboratory work will be performed under appropriate supervision and established safety procedures.

Responsibilities

- Perform hands-on electrical testing, collect measurement data, evaluate results against requirements, and clearly document test configurations and findings.
- Support environmental design-validation testing, including temperature, humidity, altitude, vibration, and mechanical shock testing, as applicable.
- Write, debug, and maintain test programs, instrument-control scripts, test sequences, data-logging routines, and analysis tools.
- Assist with the design, assembly, and validation of automated test sets used for design validation and production test.
- Control laboratory instruments using common test-and-measurement interfaces and software environments such as Python, C#, MATLAB, or VBA.
- Assist with troubleshooting across test software, instruments, fixtures, wiring, custom interface hardware, and the device under test.
- Follow established laboratory procedures and high-voltage/high-power safety practices while working under the direction of qualified engineers.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering or electrical engineering technology
- Coursework or project experience in analog circuits, digital systems, electronics, instrumentation, or measurement techniques.
- Programming experience through coursework, laboratory assignments, personal projects, internships, or student design teams.
- Working knowledge of at least one programming or engineering environment, such as Python, C#, C/C++, LabVIEW, MATLAB, or VBA.
- Interest in design validation, automated testing, laboratory instrumentation, and hands-on hardware/software problem solving.
- Ability to analyze data, communicate technical results, and create clear engineering documentation.
- Ability to work safely and carefully in a laboratory environment and follow written test procedures.
- Experience with laboratory instruments such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, power analyzers, or data-acquisition equipment.

Preferred Qualifications

- Exposure to instrument automation using SCPI commands, VISA, serial communications, Ethernet, USB, or GPIB.
- Coursework, project, or internship exposure to power electronics, high-voltage systems, regenerative power supplies, electronic loads, or high-power test equipment.
- Experience with PCB schematic capture or layout tools and basic board bring-up or soldering.
- Experience with 3D modeling software such as NX, Creo, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or an equivalent tool.
- Exposure to environmental testing, test chambers, data analysis, source control, or structured software development practices.
- Participation in engineering clubs or project teams such as Formula SAE, robotics, solar car, IEEE, or capstone design.

About Basis

Basis is a nonprofit applied AI research organization with two mutually reinforcing goals.

The first is to understand and build intelligence. This means to establish the mathematical principles of what it means to reason, to learn, to make decisions, to understand, and to explain; and to construct software that implements these principles.

The second is to advance society’s ability to solve intractable problems. This means expanding the scale, complexity, and breadth of problems that we can solve today, and even more importantly, accelerating our ability to solve problems in the future.

To achieve these goals, we’re building both a new technological foundation that draws inspiration from how humans reason, and a new kind of collaborative organization that puts human values first.

About the Role

Research interns work closely with scientists and engineers at Basis, learning from and contributing to our team. Internships are open to graduate-level candidates (or equivalent), pursuing research in technical and scientific domains, including areas of computer science such as machine learning, and programming languages.

We are looking for people who want to grow technically and who value gaining a deeper understanding of concepts at their foundations.

We expect you to:

- Have demonstrated an ability to do high-quality scientific research. Possible ways to demonstrate this include publications, technical reports, and software projects

In addition, the following would be an advantage:

- Excited about solving real world problems and having positive societal impact

Activities

- Develop and explore computational theories of intelligence, including reasoning, learning, and decision-making

- In close collaboration with domain experts inside and especially outside Basis, work as a team member to help solve scientific and societal problems

- Distill insights from solving problems into more general mathematical and computational theories

- Contribute to open-source software

- (Optionally) Publish and present findings in journals and conferences

- Contribute to the culture and direction of Basis

Potential projects

Interns will be placed with one of our active challenge projects or our core tech team, according to project needs and intern fit. In particular, we have openings within the following areas, but this list is not exhaustive:

- Dynamical Systems + Machine Learning at Basis

- We’re seeking interns interested in developing the theory and methods that let us learn how systems work from data—and quantify what we don’t know. This work sits at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, and uncertainty quantification, with the goal of advancing how we represent, infer, and forecast complex real-world processes under uncertainty.

- Projects may be theoretical (developing foundations for learning and reasoning about dynamics), methodological or engineering-focused (building and integrating algorithms into our universal reasoning engine), or applied (using our existing toolkits to study systems such as animal behavior and robot co-design).

- Recent blogpost: Introducing Dynestyx, a probabilistic programming library for dynamical systems

- Interns should have familiarity with differential equations, machine learning, and Bayesian inference.

- Secure Sensing & Robotics

- We are starting a new hardware research effort on privacy-centered hardware. The ubiquity of IoT devices and never-ending appetite of large-scale AI models have normalized mass data recording and mining of public and private spaces. This motivates numerous research questions: (1) how do we design public interest IoT and robotics applications that preserve community members’ privacy? (2) How can we design checks and balances in sensing systems to affirm compliance with consent and anti-eavesdropping laws? (3) How do we center trustworthiness in the design of IoT and robotic system? We are looking for candidates with experience in at least one of the following: embedded systems, edge computing, robotics, machine learning, security, and computer vision. Please feel free to reach out to learn more about the latest work.

- Formal Methods and Verification

- Basis is building infrastructure for machine-checkable trust in scientific software and autonomous systems. Our aim is to make it practical to express what a system should do, verify that it does it, and maintain that evidence as the system evolves.

- Recent blogposts: Synthesizing Rollback Systems for Safer Agents, Ship your interpreter, Using LLM-based verification to eliminate bugs in Linux's network stack.

- Collaborative Intelligent Systems

- We study collaborative intelligent systems in the wild, focusing on how social species coordinate, communicate, and adapt in complex environments. Our work spans multiple levels of behavior, from fine-grained group foraging and navigation decisions to city-scale ecological and evolutionary dynamics. Using multimodal data (audio, video, environmental, and genetic), we develop probabilistic and dynamical systems models that investigate how communication and cooperation shape resilience in changing ecosystems. Interns will contribute to data analysis, modeling, or field data collection for our “behavioral weather station” network monitoring social species across cities.

- Recent blogposts: Reconstructing animal movements in 3D naturalistic environments from field measurements, The hidden sounds of rats: A new way to hear urban wildlife

- Key skills: interest in animal behavior or collective systems; experience with data science, machine learning. Preference will be given to candidates with experience in at least one of the following areas: dynamical systems modeling, multimodal data analysis, multi-agent simulation.

- MARA – Modeling, Abstraction & Reasoning Agents

- Science advances by discovering useful abstractions. MARA operationalizes this insight into software agents. Instead of passively absorbing data, MARA agents propose hypotheses, run physical or simulated experiments, and revise models of the world until a compact, coherent theory emerges. Early results show MARA systems solving previously unresolved (ARC) Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus tasks; widely considered among the hardest AI benchmarks today. We are also opening a new branch of the project to bring MARA into the physical world, with embodied agents (robots) that learn from experience, build internal representations, and apply "everyday science" human-like reasoning to solve problems.

- Recent blogposts: ExoPredicator: abstracting time and state for robot planning, AutumnBench: world model learning in humans and AI

Role Details

- FT/PT: This is a full-time position.

- Start and end dates: This is typically a summer position but the dates are flexible. The internship should span at least three months.

- Location: This is an in-person position in either the New York City or Boston/Cambridge area.

- Salary: $100,000 annually

- Application close date:

- We will begin reviewing applications for Summer 2027 in November 2026, and the application will remain open until the cohort is full.

Your information may be processed in different countries, including the US. You retain copyright while providing Basis a license to use these materials for the stated purposes.

The Regulated Bioanalytical Sciences team is advancing laboratory digital transformation by improving how assay workflows and experimental data are captured, structured, and managed within Benchling. The intern will support a digital transformation project aimed at converting prioritized Test Method (TM) documents into standardized Benchling templates. Benchling serves as the Regulated Bioanalytical Sciences laboratory information management system used to capture, organize, and manage structured experimental workflows and data.

Activities may include reviewing Test Methods to identify workflow steps, data fields, and calculations, and translating those elements into structured Benchling templates supported by clear documentation.
